watchOS 27 will launch this fall as the next major software update for Apple Watch, and it introduces a useful new feature that can extend your Apple Watch's battery life—the "Active Battery Extension Notification."

watchOS 27 can proactively extend Apple Watch battery life by disabling features you don't use

watchOS 27 is coming soon, bringing two brand-new apps to Apple Watch, a useful tap gesture, new default watch faces, three health-related upgrades, and much more.

Another new feature in watchOS 27 aims to improve your Apple Watch's battery life.

"Active Battery Extension Notification" is a brand-new type of alert you might see on your Apple Watch.

When you receive a battery extension notification, it means watchOS 27 has detected that you have several features you've never used, and disabling them could save battery life.

These features include various gestures, the "Raise to Speak" function that activates Siri, and "Start Workout" reminders, among others.

Each of these features involves background processing and places some drain on battery life.

Therefore, in watchOS 27, if the system detects that you've never used these features, it will automatically disable them. The system will issue a "Battery Extension Notification" to inform you that this action is being taken, while also giving you the option to keep them enabled.

If you regularly use these features, you'll never see this prompt. Of course, you can always open Settings to manually disable these features in exchange for longer battery life.

Apple hasn't specifically stated how much additional battery life users can gain by disabling these features. But it's clear that the power savings are significant enough to warrant building this entirely new battery extension feature.

Have you tried features like Apple Watch's "Raise to Speak," gestures, or "Start Workout" reminders? Will you keep them enabled going forward? Let us know your thoughts in the comments.
